historical_names.date_source_note: Oil camp founded by British Controlled Oilfields
historical_names.name: Mene de Mauroa

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 23 June 1892 by Eugenio Alemán as Jobson around the provincial railway station in Vera Department, Santa Fe.
historical_names.name: Jobson

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially renamed Vera in 1954 upon attaining city status, adopting the name of Vera Department and its railway station.
historical_names.name: Vera

historical_names.date_source_note: Created as Distrito de Campo Verde in Coronel Portillo Province, Ucayali, on 1 June 1982 (Ley N° 23416).
historical_names.name: Campo Verde

historical_names.date_source_note: Cantonisation of Cantón Pangua in Cotopaxi Province on 31 May 1938, preserving the indigenous Panzaleo/Kichwa toponym Pangua (cantonal seat at El Corazón).
historical_names.name: Pangua

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Muchik settlement and cacicazgo in the Lambayeque valley, continuously retaining its indigenous name through the 16th-century Spanish colonial reducción and Peruvian republican district era.
historical_names.name: Mochumí

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded by Captain Buenaventura de Bustos Baquero
historical_names.name: San Buenaventura de Ejido

historical_names.date_source_note: Shortened republican town name
historical_names.name: Ejido

historical_names.date_source_note: Urban parish Ignacio Fernández Peña created in Ejido
historical_names.name: Fernández Peña

historical_names.date_source_note: Modern oil town emerged following the completion of Venezuela's first commercial oil well, Zumaque I (MG-1), on 31 July 1914; 'mene' derives from the indigenous term for natural petroleum seeps.
historical_names.name: Mene Grande

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial settlement and Inca gold-washing site
historical_names.name: Tiltil

historical_names.date_source_note: Original attested name of the rural paraje and finca in Anta Department, Salta, where the railway settlement consolidated around 1920 upon the advance of the Ferrocarril Central Norte (exact founding day not independently confirmed).
historical_names.name: Laguna Blanca

historical_names.date_source_note: Railway settlement and station formally designated Joaquín V. González by 1933 (following the 1931 Ferrocarril Central Norte siding and transitional provincial notices as Estación Joaquín V. González / Laguna Blanca; exact decree day not independently confirmed), honouring jurist and statesman Joaquín Víctor González; seat of Departamento Anta from 1947.
historical_names.name: Joaquín V. González

historical_names.date_source_note: Partido de Los Toldos created on 6 August 1908 by Buenos Aires Provincial Law 3106, with the town of Los Toldos (founded 2 November 1892 on lands settled since 1862 by the Mapuche community of Cacique Ignacio Coliqueo) as its seat.
historical_names.name: Los Toldos

historical_names.date_source_note: Partido de Los Toldos renamed Partido de General Viamonte in 1910 by Buenos Aires provincial law during the May Revolution Centenary (exact month and day in 1910 not independently confirmed); its municipal seat remained Los Toldos.
historical_names.name: General Viamonte

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Quechua settlement in the Sacred Valley of the Incas (royal estate zone associated with Yucay under Topa Inca Yupanqui and Huayna Capac), preceding Spanish conquest.
historical_names.name: Urupampa

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish colonial reducción formally founded in 1572 in the Yucay Valley under Viceroy Francisco de Toledo's general resettlement (executed by Lic. Pedro Gutiérrez Flores; exact day not independently confirmed), hispanicising Quechua Urupampa; the later parish dedication to San Pedro Apóstol subsequently gave rise to the ecclesiastical form San Pedro de Urubamba.
historical_names.name: San Bernardo de Urubamba

historical_names.date_source_note: Constituted as capital of the Province of Urubamba by decree of Simón Bolívar on 21 June 1825 (later titled Benemérita Ciudad de Urubamba on 9 November 1839).
historical_names.name: Urubamba

historical_names.date_source_note: Urban town founded on 8 December 1907 by Benjamín Zubiaurre alongside Estación Divisadero as the seat of Partido del Tuyú (created in 1865).
historical_names.name: Divisadero

historical_names.date_source_note: Renamed General Juan Madariaga by Buenos Aires Provincial Law N.º 3261 (sanctioned 8 August 1910, promulgated 11 August 1910), superseding Divisadero and Partido del Tuyú.
historical_names.name: General Juan Madariaga

historical_names.date_source_note: Municipio de 18 de Mayo newly created on 20 March 2013 by Junta Departamental de Canelones Decreto N° 62/2013 (approved 19 March 2013) out of suburban barrios of Las Piedras and Progreso, named after the historic AFE railway halt Parada 18 de Mayo (commemorating the 18 May 1811 Battle of Las Piedras); formally declared a city by Uruguayan Law 19.543 on 20 October 2017.
historical_names.name: 18 de Mayo

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 8 October 1886 along the Ferrocarril Buenos Aires al Pacífico in southern Córdoba, named in honour of French jurist Édouard René de Laboulaye.
historical_names.name: Laboulaye

historical_names.date_source_note: Settlement consolidated near Capacho Nuevo after earthquake
historical_names.name: El Valle

historical_names.date_source_note: Civil parish created in Independencia Municipality
historical_names.name: Juan Germán Roscio

historical_names.date_source_note: Agricultural settlement and rural parish of San Carlos in the Naranjal–Cañar borderland, incorporated within Cantón Naranjal upon its creation on 7 November 1960 (no documented historical rename).
historical_names.name: San Carlos

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial reducción and parish organised in Chayanta (Charcas) under Viceroy Francisco de Toledo's general resettlement (c. 1572–1575; exact day not independently confirmed), attested in colonial ecclesiastical and mining records of Charcas as San Salvador de Ocurí (Asiento de Minas de San Salvador de Ocurí).
historical_names.name: San Salvador de Ocurí

historical_names.date_source_note: Formally listed under the shortened republican civil name Cantón Ocurí within Chayanta Province by the Bolivian Law of 3 September 1880 reorganising Chayanta and Charcas (having already figured as a canton in 19th-century republican Chayanta), and later constituted as an autonomous municipality (Fourth Municipal Section of Chayanta Province) by Law 257 of 16 November 1963.
historical_names.name: Ocurí

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial indigenous settlement (Calamarí/Mokaná territory in the hinterland of Cartagena) documented prior to Spanish colonisation and preceding the colonial town of Santa Rosa.
historical_names.name: Alipaya

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial parish established c. 1735 on the site of indigenous Alipaya in the Province of Cartagena (attested in the 1778–1779 Cartagena provincial census); known concurrently as Santa Rosa and Santa Rosa de Lima without a separate modern rename.
historical_names.name: Santa Rosa

historical_names.date_source_note: Settlement established c. 1872–1876 (exact day not independently confirmed) by Afro-Colombian settlers acquiring plots on lands of the historical hacienda of Guachené within the jurisdiction of Caloto, Cauca (continuing the indigenous toponym associated with Cacique Guachené); long administered as a corregimiento of Caloto before gaining municipal autonomy on 19 December 2006 by Decreto Ordenanza 0653 of the Governor of Cauca.
historical_names.name: Guachené

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Zenú indigenous settlement (site of the Momil archaeological complex and Cacique Momil) on the Ciénaga Grande del Bajo Sinú, preceding Spanish colonisation.
historical_names.name: Momil

historical_names.date_source_note: Refounded and reorganised as a Spanish colonial settlement on 17 November 1776 by Antonio de la Torre y Miranda under the name San Antonio de Momil in the Province of Cartagena.
historical_names.name: San Antonio de Momil

historical_names.date_source_note: Formally constituted as Municipio de Momil in Córdoba Department by Departmental Ordenanza 021 of 21 August 1963 (segregated from Purísima), establishing the shortened modern official municipal name (used earlier in republican administration alongside San Antonio de Momil).
historical_names.name: Momil

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial reducción and parish founded in the Corregimiento of Larecaja (Kallawaya valley region, La Paz) under Viceroy Francisco de Toledo's general resettlement (c. 1572–1575; exact day not independently confirmed), documented in colonial ecclesiastical and visita records as San Pedro de Mocomoco.
historical_names.name: San Pedro de Mocomoco

historical_names.date_source_note: Incorporated as Cantón Mocomoco within the newly created Province of Muñecas by Bolivian Law of 18 October 1826 (signed by President Antonio José de Sucre, dividing Larecaja), establishing the shortened republican civil name (later transferred to Eliodoro Camacho Province by Law of 5 November 1908).
historical_names.name: Mocomoco

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 4 August 1791 as a Franciscan mission settlement along the Uchiza River in the Alto Huallaga by Fray Manuel Sobreviela (Guardian of the Colegio de Ocopa) with 16 Cholón families, contemporaneously documented in Mercurio Peruano (1791); later constituted as Distrito de Uchiza by Peruvian Law 1595 on 21 October 1912.
historical_names.name: Uchiza

historical_names.date_source_note: Constituted as Departamento de Perico del Carmen in 1851 around the 18th-century chapel settlement of Nuestra Señora del Carmen in the Valle de Perico, Jujuy (recorded as Perico del Carmen in the 1869 and 1895 Argentine national censuses).
historical_names.name: Perico del Carmen

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially designated El Carmen by the early 20th century, as recorded in the Third Argentine National Census of 1 June 1914 (shortened from Perico del Carmen to distinguish it from Estación Perico; exact provincial decree date between 1895 and 1914 not independently confirmed).
historical_names.name: El Carmen

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded by Fray Manuel de Úbeda
historical_names.name: Santísima Trinidad de los Porongos

historical_names.date_source_note: Designated capital of Flores Department as Trinidad
historical_names.name: Trinidad

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial indigenous settlement east of Cumaná
historical_names.name: Nuestra Señora del Socorro

historical_names.date_source_note: Traditional eastern coastal barrio of Cumaná
historical_names.name: Caigüire

historical_names.date_source_note: Urban parish created in Sucre Municipality
historical_names.name: Valentín Valiente

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 24 March 1950 by José Francisco Rojas Guerra along the Troncal de Occidente highway in the San Jorge subregion (then part of Ayapel); later elevated to an independent municipality of Córdoba Department by Departmental Ordinance 010 of 13 November 1969.
historical_names.name: Buenavista

historical_names.date_source_note: Settled and founded as Balboa in 1912 in the Patía region of Cauca (named after Vasco Núñez de Balboa; exact month and day not independently confirmed), later elevated to an independent municipality in 1967.
historical_names.name: Balboa

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 15 August 1563 in the Upano Valley (Shuar and Macas indigenous territory) as Nuestra Señora del Rosario de Macas; survivors of the 1599 destruction of nearby Sevilla de Oro later consolidated here.
historical_names.name: Nuestra Señora del Rosario de Macas

historical_names.date_source_note: Designated Macas (Cantón Macas) in the 25 June 1824 Ley de División Territorial of Gran Colombia, establishing the modern republican name (now capital of Morona Santiago Province and Cantón Morona).
historical_names.name: Macas

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial indigenous Panzaleo/Sigchos chiefdom in the western highlands of Cotopaxi, preceding Spanish colonisation.
historical_names.name: Sigchos

historical_names.date_source_note: Established as the Spanish colonial parish (doctrina) of San Miguel de Sigchos within the Corregimiento of Latacunga in the late 16th century (exact founding day not independently confirmed).
historical_names.name: San Miguel de Sigchos

historical_names.date_source_note: Formally constituted as the civil parish of Sigchos under Ecuador's Ley de División Territorial of 29 May 1861 (elevated to Cantón Sigchos on 21 July 1992).
historical_names.name: Sigchos

historical_names.date_source_note: Early fishing and estate settlement north of Maracaibo
historical_names.name: Cabeza de Toro

historical_names.date_source_note: Urban parish created in Maracaibo Municipality
historical_names.name: Idelfonso Vásquez
